- When sentiment is high (≥0.53) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.27) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts late-period (last 10 days) prices; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for days 20–30.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative (e.g., 0.80 → 0.00), model fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of price decline), model overreacts; apply 0.5–1.5% upward correction to avoid underestimating rebound.
